pages.aboutBody:
Zhovten Games is an independent game studio founded in December 2025 by Oksana Dubinetska and Sam Starling. We work where narrative game design, gameplay systems, web engineering, technical experimentation, and public research meet.

posts.title: Brain Anatomy & Information Flow: Interim Update
posts.description: Interim update linked to the Brain Anatomy & Information Flow research publication.
posts.body:
Hello everyone.

This month’s update is an interim update ahead of a larger release. It is forced on purpose, because it is tied to a special date.

I will wrap it in a short comedic remark in the spirit of “our Dr. Samuel,” who cannot quite communicate with an audience like a normal person, but is trying:

> — Hey, how is the game coming along?  
> — We are doing stats!  
> — Sounds like you have come a long way. Anything to show?  
> — Enjoy.

[Brain Anatomy & Information Flow — Practical Primer](https://github.com/Zhovten-Games/InterDeadReferenceLibrary/blob/fdc344b10bc3367bcb3a4701e6cc08c7e3dea1f2/research/brain_anatomy/Brain%20Anatomy%20%26%20Information%20Flow%20(Practical%20Primer).md)

I started writing this overview in parallel with the early work on the framework that helped us build an inverted fear table. That line later became part of [PsyFramework](/blog/psyframework-screening-prototype/). Initially, the document was meant for internal use, but it turned out interesting enough that we decided to publish it.

“We are doing stats” partially explains why this text exists, but it does not fully explain the logic behind it. We will make the full picture explicit later.

If you are curious to watch how it all assembles into something coherent, we plan to integrate into the website the first version of the app — the one everything started with — and the one we already discussed in *Echo of an Unfading Memory*:

- [English](https://interdead.phantom-draft.com/about/)

posts.title: Canon Horror Series: Language as Infection and the Systems of Horror
posts.description: Research-track announcement for Canon Horror Series: Language as Infection.
posts.body:
How a game sometimes develops a research side track.

Earlier in *Echo of an Unfading Memory*, we wrote that one of the core lines behind InterDead emerged against the background of war and an attempt to rethink language: is it possible to construct a more universal system of signs, what actually carries meaning, and where formal communication ends and lived experience begins.

Later, we showed how the philosophical “Why” was turned into an operational canon structure through a public wiki and SSOT approach. Within that same public wiki layer, we formalized Emoji Protocol — our “language of the dead,” where communication operates through a constrained set of symbols, response contracts, ACK logic, and the constant risk of misinterpretation.

From these internal discussions, a side research track emerged, framed as **Language as Infection — Media Communication as a Mechanism of Harm**.

[Initial public research snapshot](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19773963)

The current corpus includes:

- *Language as Infection — Media Communication as a Mechanism of Harm*
- *After the Nuclear Strike — The Transformation of Japanese Horror from Monster to Infected System*
- *When Disaster Becomes Environment — Chernobyl and the Spatial Model of Horror*
- *Viruses and Bioweapons — Infection Mechanics and Media Analogues*

All materials are published as bilingual working papers / preprints and are not peer reviewed.

We have also prepared a journal version of the work and plan to release it publicly soon. So if the idea resonates but four papers already feel like excessive cognitive load, a more compressed version is coming.

## Key references

Echo of an Unfading Memory — In Place of an About InterDead:

- [English](https://interdead.phantom-draft.com/about/)

[doi.org/10.1016/j.chbr.2025.100750](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chbr.2025.100750)

[Leibniz 1666 conspect](https://github.com/Zhovten-Games/InterDeadReferenceLibrary/blob/0976d1b600fa3b2b0fc3461ff524d38c65c71fc1/research/leibniz_1666_conspect/Leibniz%20(1666)%20-%20a%20glossary%20of%20source%20terms%20and%20a%20brief%20explanation.md)

posts.title: Echo of an Unfading Memory: First Chapter Opened
posts.description: Announcement of the first public chapter of Echo of an Unfading Memory.
posts.body:
**Echo of an Unfading Memory** is not a reference document and not a presentation. It is a working collection that captures the internal logic of InterDead: its principles, structure, and ways of thinking.

The full version will become available after the game’s release. For now, we deliberately open only the first chapter — in place of the familiar “About us.”

Inside:

- the genesis of the project;
- the logic behind the application-prototype at its core;
- the approach we use to operationalize fear without turnkey psychometrics;
- the practical contour of how mini-games form a player profile that can later inform dramaturgy, pacing, and presentation.

Our expectation is simple: to build a psychologically oriented horror game that remains coherent, careful, and measurable, without reducing the player to a label.

Read the first chapter:

- [English](https://interdead.phantom-draft.com/about/)
- [Russian](https://interdead.phantom-draft.com/ru/about/)

posts.title: February Umbrella Update
posts.description: Umbrella update covering canon, pipeline, communication architecture, and TTRPG testing.
posts.body:
Hello everyone.

February in InterDead was not about individual publications. It was about a systemic restructuring of the project.

We finalized three architectural layers.

## 1. Canon as a Contract

We formalized the “Why” and reinforced canon discipline through a public wiki and SSOT.

Read more:

[How We Turned the Why into a Reproducible Canon Contract for InterDead](/blog/why-canon-contract-interdead/)

## 2. Reproducible Artifact Pipeline

Video production was moved to a deterministic pipeline: ASR → LLM → FFmpeg. This reduced production time by 65–75%, while strengthening stylistic control.

Read more:

[How We Reduced Video Artifact Production Time for InterDead and Built a Reproducible Pipeline](/blog/video-artifact-pipeline-interdead/)

## 3. Communication Architecture

We unified the project voice through the system character Niro and built a cross-platform communication model.

Read more:

[How We Structured Audience Communication in InterDead Through a System Character](/blog/niro-communication-architecture/)

## 4. TTRPG Layer — Live World Testing

We are now integrating tabletop RPG sessions as a live stress-test of the canon and mechanics. This layer allows us to validate causality, tension, and narrative resilience in real time.

New reports and dedicated cases on this process are coming soon.

Next comes an intermediate update of the prototype — the starting point of the entire system. After that, the focus will shift to the game’s narrative and world development.

posts.title: How We Structured Audience Communication in InterDead Through a System Character
posts.description: Case study on cross-platform narrative communication through the constrained system character Niro.
posts.body:
*On choosing voice as an architectural decision.*

## Context

InterDead operates across several environments at once: a blog, Telegram group, Discord forum, YouTube channel, and a prototype with an embedded system assistant.

Each platform has its own constraints and audience behaviors, yet all of them are meant to convey one unified world.

The core question therefore was not what we publish, but who speaks in every environment.

## Problem

In narrative-driven projects, a conventional “product voice” tends to break immersion. Corporate tone clashes with atmosphere, direct explanations feel external to the world, and tonal mismatches across platforms create the impression of several different projects instead of one coherent system.

We needed a unified voice model that would function across all communication layers.

## Hypothesis

Our assumption was simple: if all public-facing communication is routed through a defined in-world system entity, then atmosphere can be preserved across platforms, product updates can be delivered as narrative constructs, and the audience will interact not with a brand but with a diegetic layer of the world.

Consistency, in this case, becomes enforceable rather than incidental.

## Solution

The entity fulfilling this role became [Niro](https://interdead.fandom.com/wiki/Niro) — a system-level support module instantiated after [Incident NERO-01](https://interdead.fandom.com/wiki/Incident_NERO-01).

Niro operates strictly at the UI layer, is not a chat endpoint, and does not possess any “outside the system” perspective. The prototype already includes Niro, and the final game will retain this integration.



This positioning makes Niro neither a mascot nor a marketing persona, but a canon-bound system node that unifies communication through constraint.

## Fragmented Rebranding

Transitioning away from the previous stylistic layer — a heavy, Hodgson/Lovecraft-like prose imitation — triggered broader structural changes. Showcase and SEO sections were separated, categories were standardized, publication types unified, and the content plan was restructured. Contextual subtitles were added to artifacts, and a hybrid Twemoji emoji style was introduced during early iterations.

The result was a cross-platform alignment of tone and structure.

## General Communication Model

We established a single structural template for communication: consistent post types, log formats, headers, system markers, and tonal integrity. The exact same communication pattern will be reproduced inside the game, ensuring narrative continuity between the meta-layer and the in-game voice.

## Platforms

### NIRO IN NOIR Website

[InterDead blog](https://interdead.phantom-draft.com/blog/)

All publications are framed as system logs with protocol-style headers, statuses, and message-type markers. Even analytical materials are presented as structured system records — not commentary from outside the world.

### INTER{🤙🏻💀}DEAD Forum — Discord

[Discord forum](https://discord.gg/vAWYg3jFEp)

A structured, thread-based forum where discussion is encouraged, but the canon tone is preserved and deviations are minimized.

### INTER{🤙🏻💀}DEAD — Telegram

[NIRO IN NOIR discussion group](https://t.me/inter_dead)

Maintained in Ukrainian and delivered in the InterDead voice. The group name mirrors the NIRO IN NOIR structure, reinforcing the dual-layer model: an official project voice within an atmospheric wrapper.

### NIRO IN NOIR — YouTube

[YouTube channel NIRO IN NOIR](https://www.youtube.com/@inter_dead)

Only artifacts are published: no breakdowns, no out-of-character commentary, and no corporate framing. The channel visually and stylistically extends the NIRO IN NOIR blog.

## Log Standardization

Any message that risks exposing plot details or breaking the narrative frame is also formatted as a log — either system-originated or with an undefined author. This prevents tonal rupture, preserves atmosphere, and allows operational information to be published without stepping outside the diegetic frame.

## Cultural Layer

Audience interaction also operates on a cultural level: terminology, linguistic tone, and regional references. This layer is under active development and will be described in a separate case.

## Result

This approach allowed us to maintain atmospheric cohesion, unify cross-platform communication, synchronize blog, prototype, and game, and embed product information directly into narrative framing.

Niro is not a chatbot. Niro is not a brand character. Niro is a constrained system voice.

The constraint is what makes the system stable.

posts.title: Transmedia In-Universe Narrative: Approach and References
posts.description: Notes on InterDead’s transmedia in-universe narrative approach and reference model.
posts.body:
In the previous publication, we opened the first entry point into our meta-universe — a living landing page that will change together with prototypes and lore. Now, briefly and directly: the approach we chose and the examples we rely on.

**Transmedia in-universe narrative** is when parts of the story live on different media and platforms, and each part adds meaning from inside the world. It does not duplicate the same message; it expands the world. The fiction frame remains transparent and respectful to the audience. This is how our landing page works: it speaks in the voice of the world, while clearly acknowledging that it is a game.

## Examples we grew up on

- **ArkhamCare / Batman: Arkham Asylum** — an example of expanding canon through a diegetic artifact. The site lived as part of the Arkham universe, added institutional tone and archival texture, and served as a bridge between game and web environment. Terminologically: an in-universe site, a world artifact that carries new knowledge about the setting and supports its integrity.

- **13 Ghosts — Illusion-O** — the viewer chooses whether to “see” the ghosts by looking through different filters. Terminologically: audience co-participation, a gentle intensity switch placed in the viewer’s hands.

- **The Rocky Horror Picture Show** — a cult of joint viewing, rituals, props, and callbacks. Terminologically: ritualized participation, the rules of a joint game that strengthen the feeling of community.

- **Insidious: Spectral Sightings** — short web inserts about Elise’s team that expand the lore between the larger stories. Terminologically: webisode-bridges, compact autonomous parts that add texture to the world.

- **The Blair Witch Project** — a historical example of online myth-building in the late 1990s. Pulling this off “in its original form” today is unrealistic because of ethics, platform rules, and media literacy. We take from this case not deception, but the lesson of careful framing and precise world-building.

## Why do we need this?

The living landing page is our layer of “reality” inside the game. Beyond atmosphere and engagement, the landing page and a series of micro-tests will help form a player profile. Based on it, the core of the game will adapt delivery: pace, triggers, and nuances of interaction.

Simply put: you play us, and we learn how to play to you.

If this kind of play with reality resonates with you, join the discussion and prepare for the first micro-tests.

[Discord forum](https://discord.com/invite/vAWYg3jFEp)

posts.title: How We Reduced Video Artifact Production Time for InterDead and Built a Reproducible Pipeline
posts.description: Case study on reproducible InterDead artifact video production with WhisperX, LLM cues, and FFmpeg.
posts.body:
What began as an attempt to speed up the creation of short in-world videos eventually turned into a controlled, engineering-driven system that defines the visual identity of InterDead.

## Context and Objective

In InterDead, short videos function as artifacts — diegetic traces that appear both inside the application prototype, InterDeadProto, and on the project website.



To support steady content production, we needed a mechanism that would assemble these videos quickly, predictably, and with consistent stylistic rules, without re-editing each iteration by hand.

The structural formula behind all artifacts became simple:

> audio + background image + emoji overlays aligned to word-level timing

## Why Manual Editing Failed

Early attempts in Canva and Adobe Premiere Pro showed that manual assembly created a bottleneck. Each new video required full re-synchronization, stylistic consistency shifted from asset to asset, and even small revisions turned into separate micro-projects.

When we ran manual and pipeline-based production in parallel, the difference became measurable: manual editing averaged 2.5–3 hours, whereas the pipeline stabilized at 35–50 minutes. In practice, this meant a 65–75% time reduction with significantly higher consistency.

## The Roughness We Chose to Keep

Pipeline-generated videos inevitably looked more technical than manually edited ones. Surprisingly, this worked in our favor.

The artifact aesthetic survives best when it avoids polished, studio-like motion design. Although FFmpeg would allow procedural animations, and sprite-based overlays could add motion, visual restraint better supports the internal logic of InterDead.

The roughness became a feature, not a flaw.

## Pipeline Architecture

All development happens inside `InterDeadReferenceLibrary/tools/`, and the pipeline remains strictly linear and deterministic.

The process starts with [`whisperx_timing_builder`](https://github.com/Zhovten-Games/InterDeadReferenceLibrary/blob/main/tools/python_asr/whisperx_timing_builder/README.md), which takes audio input, runs WhisperX alignment, and produces an `aligned.json` file with precise word timings. Synchronizing by words — rather than lines — ensures objective, measurable cues.

The next stage is the [LLM prompt step](https://github.com/Zhovten-Games/InterDeadReferenceLibrary/blob/main/prompts/emoji-cue-generation-prompt-twemoji-ffmpeg-overlay-mode.md), which uses `aligned.json`, editorial blocks, templates, and the full transcript to generate a structured `cues[]` array for the overlays. If the ASR misses a fragment, the system marks it explicitly rather than inventing timing.

Full automation could assemble the final configuration automatically, but semantic control is more important than eliminating the last bit of manual oversight.

Finally, [`emoji_overlay_video_builder`](https://github.com/Zhovten-Games/InterDeadReferenceLibrary/blob/main/tools/python_ffmpeg/emoji_overlay_video_builder/README.md) takes the completed configuration and assembles the video through FFmpeg. The tool uses a fixed emoji pack, a defined safe area, stable offsets, and deterministic overlays. No timeline editor is involved — only rule-based composition.

## Supporting Assets

Music is generated via Suno. Commercial use requires an active subscription. Background images come from GPT-based generation and gradually form a recognizable palette and grain profile. Emoji rendering relies on the 72×72 Twemoji PNG set, which offers deterministic cross-platform consistency.

## Outcome

The pipeline is not “AI for the sake of AI.” It is a disciplined production method that shortens repetitive work, enforces visual constraints, and keeps full engineering control over generative components.

The system continues to evolve, but its core principles — repeatability, predictability, and stylistic discipline — remain stable.

The full technical specification is documented here:

[Reproducible video artifact pipeline](https://github.com/Zhovten-Games/InterDeadReferenceLibrary/blob/main/pipeline/reproducible-video-artifact-pipeline.md)

posts.title: How We Turned the Why into a Reproducible Canon Contract for InterDead
posts.description: Case study on turning the canon Why into an operational SSOT contract for InterDead.
posts.body:
*On the great and terrible Why in game design.*

## Context

InterDead operates at the intersection of narrative architecture and mechanical implementation, where the number of entities, protocols, and localizations continually grows. In such an environment, every element interacts with many others, creating a cumulative complexity effect.

## Problem

Early on, this created typical risks for a complex narrative system. Local decisions emerged without shared causality, meanings were duplicated, terminology was interpreted differently by different contributors, and internal contradictions multiplied as the canon expanded. Multilingual support further complicated consistency. In short, the project was scaling faster than the discipline required to maintain it.

## Hypothesis

We proposed that if the canon is moved into a public wiki and each entity receives an explicit “Why,” the entire structure becomes more manageable. Canon updates could be introduced in waves, causality would become verifiable, team synchronization would accelerate, and localizations would become derivative rather than autonomous versions.

## Solution

The goal was to turn the “Why” from a philosophical notion into an operational tool. It became a canon contract.

Every entity is now required to have:

- a defined purpose;
- documented causal links;
- a clear scope of applicability;
- describable consequences.

The wiki serves both as a formalization environment and as a system of constraints that enforces discipline.

## Effect Metrics

This is not a quantitative case; its impact is architectural. The approach brought predictability during scaling, reduced internal contradictions, minimized semantic divergence between localizations, and accelerated decision-making. Most importantly, it provided full control over causality.

Additional side effects included faster editorial processes and improved audience engagement — the latter addressed separately in the case “How We Offset Development Costs.”

## Limitations

The approach is not universal. It raises the entry threshold, requires terminological discipline, and slows spontaneous iteration. For projects based on rapid prototyping without a long-term canon, this level of structure may be excessive.

## Self-Discipline as the Core Factor

The model works only if every decision is required to answer “Why,” the canon is fixed before scaling, and the public nature of the wiki acts as pressure toward formulation precision. Creativity becomes structured rather than constrained.

## Model Architecture

### SSOT: Single Source of Truth

There is one primary version of the canon — in our case, English. All other localizations are derivative, which eliminates disputes over which version is “correct.”

### Change-list Process

Any change to the canon follows a clear sequence:

1. defining the “Why”;
2. identifying all affected pages;
3. updating the core material;
4. propagating dependent edits in waves;
5. verifying localizations.

This prevents chaotic edits.

### Three Publication Modes

We distinguish between manual publication, semi-automated builds, and full API synchronization via Action API + CI.

Manual publication is flexible but error-prone. Semi-automated builds reduce copy-paste. Full API synchronization offers high synchronicity and scalability. API automation includes separation of localizations, a unified format, a CI pipeline, diff logic, and token/rate-limit management. Automation, however, does not eliminate editorial responsibility during semantic changes.

## Next Stage

The next layer of complexity is cultural canon adaptation — preserving the “Why” while shifting cultural context. This will be covered in a separate case.

## Conclusion

By making the internal system public during development, we turned the “Why” into a contract, an editorial filter, an architectural stabilizer, and a synchronization mechanism — not an abstraction but an actionable part of production.

## Operational Implementation

The full operational model is documented here:

[InterDead reproducible canon pipeline](https://github.com/Zhovten-Games/InterDeadReferenceLibrary/blob/main/pipeline/Ireproducible-canon-pipeline.md)

posts.title: Zhovten Games and InterDead Launch Announcement
posts.description: Studio launch announcement and first public entry point to the InterDead meta-universe.
posts.body:
Hello everyone.

We are **Zhovten Games** — a small studio founded in October 2025 by two people.

We are creating a narrative-driven speculative fiction horror game in a novella-style format, with a set of unusual mechanics we hope will pleasantly surprise you. Our target for the demo release is Halloween 2026. Until then, we will share prototypes, art drops, dev notes, and short teasers.

At a glance:

- cross-platform;
- languages: English, Українська, 日本語;
- influences: Japanese horror — *Kairo / Pulse* and *Silent Hill* — interpreted through a speculative-fiction lens, with an intentionally austere, system-focused tone.

Today we are also launching the first entry point into the game’s meta-universe: a living landing page that will evolve with prototypes, lore breadcrumbs, and small experiments.

Explore it here: [InterDead](https://interdead.phantom-draft.com/)

authors.name: Sam Starling
authors.role: Co-Founder · Full-Stack Web Engineer · Gameplay Systems & Technical Design
authors.description: Co-founder of Zhovten Games shaped by production systems, client work, and applied engineering, now focused on web infrastructure, gameplay systems, technical design, and research.
authors.body:
Business and real applied work forged my engineering practice: support queues, broken systems, production deadlines, client risk, and decisions that had to survive contact with users. I entered IT at 18 in 2011 through technical support at uCoz, turning unclear reports into reproducible cases, diagnostics, and Jira workflows.

From there I moved through QA and product quality: functional testing, defect reproduction, system-behavior analysis, and direct work with developers. Later, at Scuba Space, I led a bilingual copywriting team and built its workflow, editorial review, and content-quality control.

Since 2019, my main field has been full-stack web engineering: client and server development, WordPress, Laravel, APIs, webhooks, deployment, architecture, security, and technical consulting. Production taught me a blunt rule: a system is defined by what continues to work after the presentation ends.

At Zhovten Games, I work on web infrastructure, gameplay systems, technical design, prototypes, narrative/game logic, and the research pipelines behind our projects. My current engineering profile and active work are documented on [GitHub](https://github.com/pan-canon).

authors.body:
I loved reading from childhood. I moved into senior school ahead of schedule and graduated with honors, then earned a Bachelor’s degree in Translation at Kyiv National Linguistics University (2014–2018) and studied at Kyiv School of Journalism in 2017.

I began working in copywriting while still young. That path led from research and commercial writing to scripts, game mastering, and finally game design—the field where narrative, systems, and production became one discipline. I am now increasingly focused on the technical side of games: quest logic, interactive structure, implementation constraints, and collaboration between narrative, art, and code.

## Experience

### [Zhovten Games](https://www.linkedin.com/company/109201497/) — Lead Game Designer / Founder

**December 2025 — present**

I shape game concepts, narrative systems, quest logic, production documentation, and cross-disciplinary implementation. My current work extends into technical game design and the boundary between design, Unity, and engineering.

### GrandMA Studios — Game Designer

**October 2021 — December 2025 · Kyiv, Ukraine**

Led narrative development for multiple HOPA titles from synopsis to final release. Wrote scripts, quest flows, interactive sequences, object descriptions, and character dialogue. Built branching narrative logic for puzzles, investigations, and quest chains while preserving UX clarity. Collaborated with artists and programmers to align story, mechanics, pacing, and environmental storytelling. Published five games across the Whispered Secrets and Mystery Case Files franchises. *Mystery Case Files: The Dalimar Legacy* reached #2 in the publisher’s all-time PC bestseller list.

### Clockwork Magick — Game Master

**October 2020 — August 2021 · Kyiv, Ukraine**

Created complete scenarios, distinctive characters, locations, and living non-player characters. Adapted game systems to the needs of each story, playtested original systems, and revised them from observed play.

### Rocketslides — Presentation and Advertising Scriptwriter

**July 2020 — June 2021**

Wrote scripts for videos, talks, and presentations in collaboration with a designer, and prepared production briefs for design and layout.

### SM Banking Club — Copywriter

**April 2019 — March 2020**

Studied English-language research on mobile banking and turned it into structured analytical reviews.
